page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard3.Flex.16-256 is an x86_64 compute instance designed for memory-intensive enterprise applications within the flexible Standard shape family. The server provides 16 physical cores and 32 dedicated vCPUs driven by an Intel Xeon 8358 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz, paired with two hardware execution threads per core. Memory allocation is set at 256.0 GB total, delivering 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

The configuration contains no bundled local storage, requiring attached network-based block volumes for persistent operating system and data storage needs. In addition, the instance operates without hardware graphics acceleration, featuring a GPU count of zero. Connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Resource scaling in the Flex model allows predictable resource reservation via dedicated CPU allocation rather than burstable or shared thread execution.

With its 1:8 core-to-memory ratio, VM.Standard3.Flex.16-256 provides significant memory density relative to core count without the operational overhead of dedicated bare-metal hardware. This profile makes the instance suitable for large in-memory caches, relational and NoSQL databases, memory-heavy enterprise resource planning systems, ETL data transformation pipelines, and high-concurrency web serving environments.

By offering dedicated CPU allocation and substantial memory capacity, this instance delivers reliable resource distribution for memory-constrained applications.
